handbookNote: Montana Real Estate Broker license exam. Part of the 2026-09-03 R26 population-tier broker buildout (population order: UT > NV > IA > AR > KS > MS > ID > NE > WV > HI > NH > MT > RI > DE > SD > ND > AK > VT > WY). Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Montana Board of Realty Regulation (Candidate Handbook #092700, January 2026). National/general portion: 80 scored items + 5 unscored pretest, 150 minutes. Montana state portion: 40 scored items (same total for Broker and Salesperson, only the per-section split differs) + 5-10 unscored pretest, 90 minutes. Combined: 120 scored items, 240 minutes. Passing score is a SCALED score of 75 (0-100 scale, NOT a raw percent-correct threshold -- the handbook explicitly states the reported score is 'neither the number of questions answered correctly nor the percentage'), National and State scored/passed INDEPENDENTLY (retake only the failed part). track_registry models this as exam_question_count=120, exam_duration_sec=14400, pass_percent=75, min_correct=90 (round(120*0.75)), same convention as every other scaled-score Pearson VUE state in this campaign (UT/NV/KS/ID/NE/WV/WY/AK/DE/RI). NATIONAL PORTION (80 items, 8 sections) reuses the exact same real Pearson VUE national item bank as Utah/Nevada/Kansas/Idaho/Nebraska/West Virginia/Rhode Island -- Montana's own Broker outline weights are IDENTICAL (10/8/10/15/12/9/8/8 across the same 8 sections). MONTANA STATE PORTION (40 items, real Broker item counts): The Real Estate Licensing Agency's Powers (2, incl. the generic Title 37 Ch.1 Part 3 Uniform Professional Licensing procedures shared by all MT boards -- investigations/hearings/appeals, and MCA 37-51-324's real-estate-specific $50/violation trust-account citation penalty distinct from the general $5,000/violation sanction cap), Licensing (2, MCA 37-51-301/308/309 -- license-required scope, 10-day office-relocation notice, broker-transfer sequence, Oct 31 annual expiration, 12-hr CE incl. a 4-hr supervising-broker carve-out), Requirements Governing the Activities of Licensees (26, largest section by far -- MCA 37-51-313/314 agency duties incl. Montana's distinctive 'statutory broker' default non-agency status and in-house designated-agent framework (explicitly NOT treated as dual agency), ARM 24.210.426 trust-account rules (3-business-day deposit, $1,000 personal-funds cushion), MCA 70-20-502's 3-day residential-disclosure rescission right), Additional Topics (4, incl. MCA 37-51-325's real E&O insurance minimums ($100k/$300k individual, $1M firm aggregate), Montana's own Principal Meridian/Baseline land-description system, the Montana Unit Ownership Act, and Montana's dual foreclosure regime -- 1-year judicial redemption vs. the Small Tract Financing Act's no-redemption nonjudicial deed-of-trust process), and Additional Broker Topics (6, Broker-only -- trust accounts/supervision/place of business/8-year recordkeeping retention/closing-statement accounting duties). Governing law: MCA Title 37, Chapter 51 (Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons) and ARM Title 24, Chapter 210 (Board of Realty Regulation). Real, confirmed finding: Montana's Real Estate Recovery Fund was REPEALED in 2019 (HB 376, all of MCA 37-51-501 through -512 individually marked repealed) -- consumer protection today runs through the mandatory E&O insurance requirement (MCA 37-51-325) instead, NOT a fund and NOT a surety bond (a genuinely distinct 3rd consumer-protection model in this campaign, alongside HI/ND/RI/DE/AK/WY's recovery funds and NH's surety bond). This bank was drafted across 5 new state-topic drafting passes (the 8 national files were reused, not redrafted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_broker_answers.js.
